message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
Here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to check |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the current AQI, pollutant levels (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), and a health‑advisory summary. |
| **AirVisual (IQAir)** | Go to <https://www.iqair.com/usa/california/los-angeles> or use the mobile app. It provides a real‑time AQI, forecast, and historical trends. |
| **BreezoMeter** | <https://www.breezometer.com/> offers a free widget and API for current air‑quality data. |
| **Local news & weather apps** | Many local stations (e.g., KABC, KNBC) display AQI on their weather pages. |
| **Smartphone apps** | “Air Quality Index” (iOS/Android) pulls data from EPA and other sources. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They usually pull the latest EPA data.

Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into interpreting AQI values or how to mitigate exposure!
